answers.answer: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 4.2% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.

steps: The simulation models what would happen if there were genuinely no difference.
Out of 500 simulated trials, 21 were at least as extreme as the observed result, a proportion of 4.2%.
Compare that against the conventional 5% threshold.
Because 4.2% is below 5%, the observed result would rarely arise by chance alone, so it is statistically significant.
